data.title: Architecture and structural dynamics of the AROM complex
data.projectDescription: Cross-linking/mass spectrometry was used to study inter-domain interactions in the multifunctional AROM complex from Chaetomium thermophilum.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking using the lysine reactive DSS was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). The cross-linked complex was digested using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin, and the digest was analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Elite system after fractionation by size exclusion chromatography. Duplicate injections for each SEC fraction were performed for precursors with a charge state of 3 and above. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of the target protein and several contaminants. Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 5 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for “common”-type fragment ions and 0.3 Da for “xlink”-type fragment ions. All candidate spectra were manually evaluated. For details, see the accompanying publication.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; hybrid structural biology
